events.title: The English East India Company receives its charter
events.summary: Elizabeth I grants a charter to a group of London merchants, giving them a monopoly over English trade east of the Cape of Good Hope.
events.detail: The company began as a joint-stock trading venture. It was not yet a territorial government, and its early voyages focused heavily on Asian maritime trade.

events.title: William Hawkins reaches Surat
events.summary: Hawkins arrives at Surat aboard the Hector during Jahangir's reign, carrying a letter from James I.
events.detail: This is commonly used as a landmark for the Company's first sustained attempt to secure trading privileges in Mughal India. English access and factory rights developed gradually rather than in a single act.

events.title: Battle of Swally (Suvali)
events.summary: An English fleet defeats a Portuguese squadron off the coast near Surat.
events.detail: The encounter helped the Company compete for maritime access on Gujarat's coast. It was a naval engagement in a wider contest involving European trading powers and Indian authorities.

events.title: English trading factory established at Surat
events.summary: The Company secures permission to establish a permanent trading presence at Surat.
events.detail: A factory was a commercial settlement, not a modern industrial plant. The Company's trading network expanded through agreements, privileges and local negotiations.

events.title: Company acquires Madras settlement
events.summary: The English obtain a grant of land on the Coromandel coast and begin developing Fort St George.
events.detail: Madras became one of the Company's principal presidencies. Its growth illustrates the Company's gradual move from coastal trade to fortified centres.

events.title: Bombay passes to the English Crown, then to the Company
events.summary: Bombay is transferred from Portugal to the English Crown as part of Catherine of Braganza's marriage settlement and leased to the Company in 1668.
events.detail: Bombay later became a major presidency and port. The Crown-to-Company transfer is distinct from the Company's original 1600 charter.

events.title: Anglo-Mughal War
events.summary: The East India Company enters open conflict with the Mughal Empire after disputes over trade and privileges.
events.detail: The Company's military position proved weak against Mughal power. The conflict ended with the Company seeking imperial pardon and resuming trade under Mughal authority.

events.title: English settlement grows at the Hooghly
events.summary: The Company consolidates settlements around Sutanuti, Govindpur and Kalikata, which later develop into Calcutta.
events.detail: The city's early formation is often associated with 1690, though its development was gradual and the role of individual founders is debated.

events.title: Company obtains zamindari rights in three Calcutta villages
events.summary: The Company acquires revenue-collecting rights over Sutanuti, Kalikata and Govindpur.
events.detail: These rights strengthened the Company's local foothold around the settlement that became Calcutta.

events.title: First Carnatic War
events.summary: A European war spills into the Carnatic, bringing French and British East India Company forces into conflict in south India.
events.detail: The war ended with the Treaty of Aix-la-Chapelle in Europe. Its Indian campaigns exposed how European rivalries could draw regional Indian powers into changing alliances.

events.title: Second Carnatic War
events.summary: British and French companies support rival claimants in Hyderabad and the Carnatic.
events.detail: The struggle was as much about succession and Indian alliances as it was about European rivalry. It helped the British strengthen their position in the south.

events.title: Third Carnatic War
events.summary: The global Seven Years' War extends to India, where British and French forces fight for influence.
events.detail: The British victory at Wandiwash in 1760 and the fall of Pondicherry in 1761 sharply reduced French political power in India.

events.title: Battle of Plassey
events.summary: Company forces under Robert Clive defeat Siraj ud-Daulah's army in Bengal after a conspiracy involving senior Bengal officials.
events.detail: The battle opened the way to Company political dominance in Bengal. Its outcome depended on defections and political bargaining as well as battlefield action.

events.title: Battle of Buxar
events.summary: Company forces defeat the combined armies of Mir Qasim, Shuja-ud-Daula and Mughal emperor Shah Alam II.
events.detail: The victory secured the Company's military position in eastern India and set up the settlement of 1765.

events.title: Treaty of Allahabad and the Diwani grant
events.summary: The Mughal emperor Shah Alam II grants the Company revenue-collecting rights (Diwani) in Bengal, Bihar and Orissa.
events.detail: The grant made the Company a major revenue authority while the nawab's institutions remained in place. It transformed a trading company into a territorial revenue power.

events.title: First Anglo-Mysore War
events.summary: Mysore under Hyder Ali fights the British East India Company and its shifting allies.
events.detail: The Treaty of Madras in 1769 restored captured territories and included a mutual-defence commitment. The treaty did not end the rivalry.

events.title: Bengal famine
events.summary: A severe famine devastates Bengal during Company revenue administration; estimates of mortality vary widely.
events.detail: The famine followed crop failure and was worsened by economic and administrative conditions. Population-loss estimates are uncertain and should not be treated as a precise count.

events.title: Regulating Act creates the Governor-General of Bengal
events.summary: The British Parliament passes the Regulating Act, creating a Governor-General of the Presidency of Fort William and a Supreme Court at Calcutta.
events.detail: Warren Hastings became the first Governor-General of Bengal. The Act marked a major step in parliamentary oversight of Company government.

events.title: First Anglo-Maratha War
events.summary: The Company and the Maratha Confederacy fight over succession and influence in western India.
events.detail: The Treaty of Salbai in 1782 restored peace and recognised Madhavrao II as Peshwa. Maratha power remained substantial after the war.

events.title: Second Anglo-Mysore War
events.summary: Hyder Ali and later Tipu Sultan fight the Company and its allies across southern India.
events.detail: The war ended with the Treaty of Mangalore in 1784, restoring much of the pre-war position. It was a major setback to the Company's efforts to dominate Mysore.

events.title: Treaty of Mangalore
events.summary: Tipu Sultan and the East India Company conclude the treaty ending the Second Anglo-Mysore War.
events.detail: The agreement restored territories and prisoners. It is notable as a negotiated settlement between Mysore and the Company.

events.title: Third Anglo-Mysore War
events.summary: The Company, the Marathas and Hyderabad fight Mysore after Tipu Sultan attacks Travancore, a British ally.
events.detail: The war ended with the Treaty of Seringapatam in 1792, under which Tipu ceded territory and paid an indemnity.

events.title: Permanent Settlement in Bengal
events.summary: The Company introduces a land-revenue system that fixes the revenue demand on zamindars in Bengal and adjoining areas.
events.detail: The arrangement reshaped landholding and rural revenue relations. Its long-term effects varied by region and are debated by historians.

events.title: Wellesley becomes Governor-General
events.summary: Richard Wellesley takes office and pursues an assertive policy of subsidiary alliances.
events.detail: The policy expanded Company influence over Indian states by tying rulers to British military and diplomatic arrangements.

events.title: Fourth Anglo-Mysore War; fall of Seringapatam
events.summary: Company-led forces storm Seringapatam; Tipu Sultan is killed and Mysore's political order is remade.
events.detail: The war ended the independent military challenge posed by Tipu's Mysore. The kingdom was restored in reduced form under the Wodeyar dynasty, with Company influence dominant.

events.title: Treaty of Bassein
events.summary: Peshwa Baji Rao II signs a subsidiary treaty with the Company.
events.detail: The treaty provoked opposition among Maratha chiefs and helped trigger the Second Anglo-Maratha War.

events.title: Second Anglo-Maratha War
events.summary: The Company fights major Maratha powers, including the Scindias and Bhonsles, after the Treaty of Bassein.
events.detail: British victories at Assaye, Delhi and Laswari expanded Company control, but the campaign did not end Maratha resistance.

events.title: Vellore Mutiny
events.summary: Indian sepoys at Vellore revolt against new military regulations and associated cultural grievances.
events.detail: The uprising was suppressed within a day. It preceded the 1857 revolt and is studied as an important early military rebellion.

events.title: Anglo-Nepalese War
events.summary: The Company and the Kingdom of Nepal fight over frontier disputes and competing claims in the Himalayan region.
events.detail: The Treaty of Sugauli in 1816 fixed a new boundary and required Nepal to accept a British resident. Nepal retained its sovereignty.

events.title: Paika Rebellion in Khurda
events.summary: Paikas and local allies rise against Company rule in Odisha amid land, revenue and political grievances.
events.detail: Bakshi Jagabandhu became a central leader. The rebellion was suppressed, but it remains an important episode of regional resistance.

events.title: Third Anglo-Maratha War
events.summary: The Company fights the Peshwa and several Maratha chiefs, bringing the Peshwa's rule to an end.
events.detail: The war dismantled the Maratha Confederacy as a major political power. Several princely states remained under British paramountcy.

events.title: First Anglo-Burmese War
events.summary: The Company fights the Burmese Konbaung kingdom over frontier expansion and influence in the northeast.
events.detail: The Treaty of Yandabo (1826) ended the war and imposed territorial cessions and an indemnity on Burma.

events.title: Treaty of Yandabo
events.summary: The treaty ends the First Anglo-Burmese War.
events.detail: Burma ceded Arakan and Tenasserim and agreed to other terms. The war was costly for the Company and reshaped the eastern frontier.

events.title: Charter Act ends the Company's commercial role in India
events.summary: Parliament removes the Company's remaining commercial functions in India and centralises legislative authority.
events.detail: The Company continued as an administrative instrument until the transfer of government in 1858; its formal dissolution came later, in 1874.

events.title: English Education Minute and policy debate
events.summary: Thomas Babington Macaulay's Minute influences the Company's decision to fund English-language education.
events.detail: The measure was part of a wider, contested education policy shift. Indigenous and vernacular learning continued, and later policy evolved.

events.title: First Anglo-Afghan War
events.summary: A British Indian army invades Afghanistan to replace Dost Mohammad Khan with Shah Shuja.
events.detail: The occupation of Kabul collapsed amid revolt; the retreat from Kabul in 1842 was catastrophic. The war ended with the British withdrawal and Shah Shuja's death.

events.title: Conquest and annexation of Sindh
events.summary: Company forces defeat the Talpur rulers of Sindh and annex the region.
events.detail: Charles Napier's campaigns at Miani and Dubbo were decisive. The annexation extended Company rule westward.

events.title: First Anglo-Sikh War
events.summary: The Company and the Sikh Empire fight across the Sutlej frontier.
events.detail: The Treaty of Lahore in 1846 imposed territorial and political changes on the Sikh state, which remained under a British resident and regency.

events.title: Second Anglo-Sikh War
events.summary: A revolt in Multan expands into a wider conflict between the Company and the Sikh Empire.
events.detail: The Company's victory led to the annexation of Punjab in 1849.

events.title: Second Anglo-Burmese War
events.summary: The Company fights Burma and annexes Pegu (Lower Burma).
events.detail: The conflict deepened British expansion into Burma, though Upper Burma remained independent until the third war in 1885.

events.title: Awadh is annexed
events.summary: The Company annexes Awadh (Oudh), citing alleged misgovernment.
events.detail: The annexation angered sections of the court, landed elite and military households. It became one of the grievances feeding the 1857 uprising.

events.title: Mangal Pandey's attack at Barrackpore
events.summary: Sepoy Mangal Pandey attacks British officers at Barrackpore; he is arrested and later executed.
events.detail: The episode became an early symbol of the 1857 uprising. The rebellion's causes were wider than the cartridge controversy and differed across regions.

events.title: Revolt begins at Meerut
events.summary: Sepoys at Meerut rebel and march towards Delhi, where Bahadur Shah Zafar becomes a symbolic figurehead.
events.detail: The uprising spread unevenly across north and central India and involved soldiers, rulers, peasants and townspeople with varied aims. It was suppressed by 1858.

events.title: Government of India Act and Queen's Proclamation
events.summary: The Act receives royal assent on 2 August; the Proclamation announcing Crown government is issued on 1 November.
events.detail: Company government ended and authority was transferred to the British Crown. Charles Canning became the first Viceroy and Governor-General under the new arrangement.

events.title: Indian Councils Act and High Courts Act
events.summary: The Crown-era administration introduces new council arrangements and establishes High Courts in the presidencies.
events.detail: These laws expanded the formal institutions of the Raj, though representative participation remained limited.

events.title: Royal Titles Act
events.summary: The British Parliament authorises the title Empress of India for Queen Victoria.
events.detail: The title formalised imperial symbolism; it did not create a new Indian representative institution.

events.title: Second Anglo-Afghan War
events.summary: British forces invade Afghanistan after tensions over foreign influence and diplomatic access.
events.detail: The Treaty of Gandamak in 1879 gave Britain influence over Afghan foreign relations. Fighting resumed after the Afghan ruler was challenged; the war concluded in 1880.

events.title: First session of the Indian National Congress
events.summary: Delegates meet in Bombay under the presidency of Womesh Chunder Bonnerjee.
events.detail: The Congress began as a platform for political discussion and petitions; over time it became a central organisation in the freedom movement, with changing strategies and constituencies.

events.title: Third Anglo-Burmese War
events.summary: British forces invade Upper Burma and depose King Thibaw.
events.detail: Upper Burma was annexed in 1886. Burma was administered as part of British India until it became a separate colony in 1937.

events.title: Anglo-Manipur War
events.summary: A succession crisis in Manipur leads to armed conflict with British forces.
events.detail: The British victory resulted in the annexation of Manipur's administration under a British political arrangement; the kingdom continued under a ruler.

events.title: Partition of Bengal takes effect; Swadeshi expands
events.summary: The Curzon government's partition of Bengal takes effect, prompting boycott, indigenous industry and public mobilisation.
events.detail: The Swadeshi movement drew in students, educators, workers, women and political organisers. The partition was annulled in 1911.

events.title: All-India Muslim League is founded
events.summary: The Muslim League is founded at Dacca during a meeting of Muslim leaders.
events.detail: Its political aims and relationship with other organisations changed over the following decades; it became a principal participant in the 1940s constitutional negotiations.

events.title: Congress split at Surat
events.summary: Differences between the so-called Moderates and Extremists culminate in a split at the Surat session.
events.detail: The split reflected debates over political methods, leadership and the pace of the national movement.

events.title: Muzaffarpur bomb attack
events.summary: Khudiram Bose and Prafulla Chaki throw a bomb at a carriage believed to carry magistrate Kingsford; two British women are killed.
events.detail: Kingsford was not in the carriage. Bose was tried and executed; Chaki died by suicide after being pursued. The episode is a stark reminder that revolutionary violence could also kill unintended victims.

events.title: Indian Councils Act (Morley–Minto reforms)
events.summary: The Act expands legislative councils and introduces separate electorates for Muslims.
events.detail: It widened formal representation while retaining strong executive control. Its effects and political meaning were contested among Indian leaders.

events.title: Bengal partition annulled; capital shift announced
events.summary: At the Delhi Durbar, the British government announces the annulment of Bengal's partition and the transfer of the imperial capital from Calcutta to Delhi.
events.detail: The reorganisation took effect over the next few years; New Delhi was formally inaugurated as the capital in 1931.

events.title: Delhi-Lahore Conspiracy attack
events.summary: A bomb is thrown at the ceremonial procession of Viceroy Lord Hardinge in Delhi.
events.detail: The plot connected underground revolutionary networks. Hardinge was injured; investigations led to trials and executions.

events.title: Ghadar movement organised overseas
events.summary: Indian migrants and political exiles organise the Ghadar movement in North America, publishing a revolutionary newspaper and advocating an uprising.
events.detail: The network linked expatriate communities with anti-colonial activism in India. Its 1915 plans were disrupted by arrests and surveillance.

events.title: Komagata Maru voyage and Budge Budge incident
events.summary: The Komagata Maru reaches Vancouver; after being denied entry, it returns to India, where a confrontation occurs at Budge Budge near Calcutta.
events.detail: The incident exposed racial exclusion in imperial migration policy and became a major event in the Ghadar-era diaspora story.

events.title: M. K. Gandhi returns to India
events.summary: Gandhi returns from South Africa and begins a period of travel and political learning in India.
events.detail: His subsequent campaigns drew on satyagraha, but the freedom movement remained plural, with constitutional, socialist, revolutionary, peasant, labour and regional currents.

events.title: Home Rule Leagues and Lucknow Pact
events.summary: Bal Gangadhar Tilak and Annie Besant organise Home Rule Leagues; Congress and the Muslim League reach the Lucknow Pact.
events.detail: The year brought renewed political cooperation and demands for self-government, though disagreements about representation and strategy continued.

events.title: Champaran Satyagraha
events.summary: Gandhi intervenes in disputes over indigo cultivation and planter coercion in Bihar.
events.detail: The campaign helped establish Gandhi as a national political figure and was shaped by local cultivators, lawyers and organisers, including Raj Kumar Shukla.

events.title: Kheda Satyagraha and Ahmedabad mill strike
events.summary: Campaigns over land revenue in Kheda and wages in Ahmedabad draw Gandhi and other organisers into local struggles.
events.detail: These actions illustrate how the movement connected national politics with specific agrarian and labour grievances.

events.title: Rowlatt Act receives assent
events.summary: The Anarchical and Revolutionary Crimes Act extends wartime emergency powers into peacetime.
events.detail: Its passage prompted widespread protest and Gandhi's first all-India satyagraha campaign.

events.title: Jallianwala Bagh massacre
events.summary: Troops under Brigadier-General Reginald Dyer fire on a large gathering in Amritsar.
events.detail: The firing killed and wounded many people. Official and other estimates differ; the episode became a turning point in public opposition to colonial rule.

events.title: Third Anglo-Afghan War
events.summary: Afghan forces cross the frontier and fighting breaks out with British India.
events.detail: The conflict ended in an armistice and subsequent agreements that recognised Afghanistan's independence in conducting its foreign relations.

events.title: Non-Cooperation Movement adopted
events.summary: Congress adopts non-cooperation, including the boycott of selected colonial institutions and promotion of swadeshi.
events.detail: The movement brought broad participation but contained different local aims. It was suspended by Gandhi in 1922 after violence at Chauri Chaura.

events.title: Malabar/Moplah Rebellion
events.summary: An uprising in Malabar combines agrarian grievances, anti-colonial mobilisation and communal violence.
events.detail: The rebellion and its aftermath were complex and violent; accounts differ in emphasis. It should not be reduced to a single-cause narrative.

events.title: Chauri Chaura incident; Non-Cooperation suspended
events.summary: A crowd in Chauri Chaura, United Provinces, sets a police station on fire, killing 22 policemen.
events.detail: Gandhi suspends the national movement, arguing that it had moved away from non-violent discipline. Other leaders disagreed with the decision.

events.title: Manyam/Rampa Rebellion begins
events.summary: Alluri Sitarama Raju and tribal fighters attack police stations in the Godavari Agency region.
events.detail: The uprising grew from grievances over forest rules and colonial administration. Its participants used guerrilla tactics; Raju was captured and killed in May 1924.

events.title: Swaraj Party is formed
events.summary: C. R. Das and Motilal Nehru organise the Swaraj Party to contest legislative councils and challenge colonial rule from within.
events.detail: The party represented a strategic disagreement within Congress about participation in colonial institutions.

events.title: Kakori train action
events.summary: Hindustan Republican Association members stop a train near Kakori and seize government funds being transported.
events.detail: The colonial prosecution led to death sentences and long imprisonments. The action helped make the HRA network widely known.

events.title: Simon Commission appointed
events.summary: The British government appoints a commission to review constitutional reforms in India, with no Indian member.
events.detail: The all-British membership triggered the slogan “Simon Go Back” and protests across India when the commission arrived in 1928.

events.title: Lala Lajpat Rai is injured during a Simon Commission protest
events.summary: Police lathi-charge a demonstration in Lahore; Lajpat Rai is injured and dies on 17 November.
events.detail: Revolutionaries held the police action responsible and planned retaliation. The causal link between the injuries and death has been debated in historical accounts.

events.title: Saunders is killed in Lahore
events.summary: Revolutionaries kill assistant superintendent J. P. Saunders, mistaking the action as retaliation for the lathi-charge on Lajpat Rai.
events.detail: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and associates were involved in the conspiracy; the event led to the Lahore Conspiracy Case.

events.title: Central Legislative Assembly bombing
events.summary: Bhagat Singh and Batukeshwar Dutt throw low-intensity bombs in the Central Legislative Assembly and distribute leaflets before surrendering.
events.detail: The action was intended as a political protest; the bombs caused no deaths. The trial gave the revolutionaries a public platform for their ideas.

events.title: Lahore Congress adopts Purna Swaraj
events.summary: The Congress session at Lahore adopts complete independence as its goal; Jawaharlal Nehru presides.
events.detail: 26 January 1930 was marked as Independence Day. The date later informed the choice of 26 January for the Constitution to come into effect in 1950.

events.title: Salt March reaches Dandi
events.summary: Gandhi and 78 original marchers leave Sabarmati Ashram on 12 March; Gandhi breaks the salt law at Dandi on 6 April.
events.detail: The march became a catalyst for civil disobedience across India. Local leaders and participants organised parallel actions in many regions.

events.title: Chittagong Armoury Raid
events.summary: Surya Sen leads a group that seizes police and auxiliary-force armouries and disrupts communications in Chittagong.
events.detail: The group failed to find ammunition but briefly disrupted colonial communications. Women including Pritilata Waddedar and Kalpana Dutta later played roles in the network.

events.title: First Round Table Conference opens
events.summary: British and Indian representatives meet in London to discuss constitutional reforms; Congress does not attend this first session.
events.detail: The conferences formed part of a longer constitutional process that culminated in the Government of India Act 1935.

events.title: Gandhi–Irwin Pact
events.summary: Gandhi and Viceroy Lord Irwin agree to suspend civil disobedience and enable Congress participation in the Second Round Table Conference.
events.detail: The pact was a negotiated pause, not a transfer of power. Its terms generated debate inside the national movement.

events.title: Bhagat Singh, Rajguru and Sukhdev are executed
events.summary: The three revolutionaries are hanged in Lahore Central Jail after conviction in the Lahore Conspiracy Case.
events.detail: Their execution became a major moment in public memory. The three had distinct roles in the wider revolutionary network.

events.title: Karachi Congress adopts a resolution on rights and economic policy
events.summary: The Congress session debates fundamental rights and national economic policy.
events.detail: The resolution is a significant document in the movement's discussion of civil liberties, labour and the shape of a future India.

events.title: Poona Pact
events.summary: B. R. Ambedkar and other leaders reach an agreement on electoral representation for the Depressed Classes after Gandhi's fast in Yerwada prison.
events.detail: The Pact replaced separate electorates proposed under the Communal Award with reserved seats in joint electorates. Its effects remain a subject of historical debate.

events.title: Government of India Act 1935 receives royal assent
events.summary: The Act provides for provincial autonomy and proposes a federation that never fully comes into operation.
events.detail: The Act became the constitutional framework for provincial elections in 1937 and influenced later constitutional arrangements.

events.title: Provincial elections under the 1935 Act
events.summary: Elections are held under the new constitutional framework and Congress ministries take office in several provinces.
events.detail: Provincial government offered limited opportunities for self-government while major powers remained with the colonial centre.

events.title: India is declared at war in World War II
events.summary: The Viceroy announces that India is at war with Germany without consulting elected Indian representatives.
events.detail: The decision intensified disputes over India's constitutional status and the conditions under which Indian resources and troops would support the war.

events.title: Lahore Resolution adopted by the Muslim League
events.summary: The Muslim League adopts a resolution calling for independent states in Muslim-majority areas of north-western and eastern India.
events.detail: The text did not use the word Pakistan; its interpretation and later political development require attention to the changing context of the 1940s.

events.title: Udham Singh is executed in London
events.summary: Udham Singh is hanged after being convicted for the 1940 killing of Michael O'Dwyer, former Lieutenant-Governor of Punjab.
events.detail: Singh said his action was connected to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre. His actions are usually situated in the revolutionary strand of anti-colonial politics.

events.title: Cripps Mission visits India
events.summary: Sir Stafford Cripps brings proposals for post-war constitutional change, which major Indian political groups do not accept.
events.detail: The failure of the negotiations contributed to the political crisis that preceded the Quit India resolution.

events.title: Quit India resolution and mass arrests
events.summary: The All India Congress Committee adopts the Quit India resolution in Bombay on 8 August; senior leaders are arrested the next day.
events.detail: The movement spread through strikes, demonstrations, underground networks and local parallel governments. Forms of action and intensity varied widely by region.

events.title: Provisional Government of Azad Hind proclaimed
events.summary: Subhas Chandra Bose announces the Provisional Government of Free India in Singapore.
events.detail: The government was associated with the Indian National Army and Axis powers during World War II. Its military campaign and political significance remain subjects of historical analysis.

events.title: Bengal famine
events.summary: A catastrophic famine strikes Bengal during World War II, causing mass death and displacement.
events.detail: The causes include wartime disruption, inflation, market failures and policy decisions; historians debate the relative weight of contributing factors.

events.title: INA campaign reaches the Imphal–Kohima frontier
events.summary: Japanese and INA forces advance into northeast India and fight Allied forces around Imphal and Kohima.
events.detail: The campaign ended in defeat for the invading forces. INA members later faced trials that drew wide attention in India.

events.title: INA trials begin at the Red Fort
events.summary: The British Indian government puts officers of the Indian National Army on trial in Delhi.
events.detail: The trials prompted broad public demonstrations and debate about loyalty, military service and independence.

events.title: Royal Indian Navy ratings' revolt begins
events.summary: Ratings in Bombay strike over conditions and raise political demands; unrest spreads to other naval establishments.
events.detail: The revolt was short-lived and involved complex political and labour grievances. It occurred amid wider unrest and negotiations over the transfer of power.

events.title: Cabinet Mission arrives
events.summary: The British Cabinet Mission holds negotiations with Congress, the Muslim League and other representatives about a constitutional settlement.
events.detail: Its plan proposed a united India with a weak centre and provincial groupings. The plan failed amid disagreements over its interpretation and implementation.

events.title: Direct Action Day and communal violence
events.summary: The Muslim League observes Direct Action Day in Calcutta; severe communal violence follows and spreads in subsequent months.
events.detail: The violence marked a grave escalation in communal conflict during the final phase of British rule. Events differed by locality and affected multiple communities.

events.title: Interim Government takes office
events.summary: An interim government is formed at the centre, with Jawaharlal Nehru as Vice-President of the Executive Council.
events.detail: The government operated within the colonial constitutional framework while negotiations over independence and partition continued.

events.title: Constituent Assembly meets for the first time
events.summary: The Constituent Assembly convenes in New Delhi to begin work on a constitution.
events.detail: The Assembly continued its work through the transfer of power and adopted the Constitution in November 1949, which came into force in January 1950.

events.title: Lord Mountbatten becomes Viceroy
events.summary: Louis Mountbatten assumes office with a mandate to oversee the transfer of power.
events.detail: The accelerated timetable culminated in the June 3 Plan and the creation of India and Pakistan in August 1947.

events.title: 3 June Plan announces partition and transfer of power
events.summary: Mountbatten announces the plan accepted by key political leaders for the partition of British India and transfer of power.
events.detail: The plan provided for the partition of Punjab and Bengal and the creation of the two Dominions. The decision was followed by extensive displacement and violence.

events.title: Indian Independence Act receives royal assent
events.summary: The British Parliament passes the Act that provides for the creation of the independent Dominions of India and Pakistan.
events.detail: The Act ended British parliamentary authority over British India and set the legal framework for the transfer of power. The princely states' position was addressed separately.

events.title: India becomes independent
events.summary: India becomes an independent Dominion; Jawaharlal Nehru takes office as the first Prime Minister.
events.detail: Independence followed a long and diverse struggle, including constitutional politics, mass movements, revolutionary activity, labour and peasant organising, military resistance and international developments. Partition accompanied the transfer.

events.title: Radcliffe boundary awards are published
events.summary: The boundary commissions' awards for Punjab and Bengal are made public two days after India's Independence Day.
events.detail: The delay meant that many people celebrated independence before learning which side of the new border their homes would fall on. Partition caused mass displacement and widespread violence.
